Negative binomial regression

nbreg.Rd

Fits a negative binomial (NB2) regression model with log link, \(\log\mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i\) and \(\mathrm{Var}(Y_i) = \mu_i + \mu_i^2/\theta\). The coefficients are estimated by iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) with \(\theta\) held fixed, alternated with Newton-Raphson updates of \(\log\theta\) with \(\beta\) held fixed, until the log-likelihood stops changing. No general-purpose optimizer is used.

Usage

nbreg(
  formula,
  data,
  offset,
  control = nbreg_control(),
  weights,
  subset,
  na.action
)

Arguments

formula

A model formula, response ~ terms. Offsets may be given with offset() terms in the formula.

data

An optional data frame containing the variables in the model.

offset

An optional vector of offsets (e.g. log exposure), added to any offset() terms in the formula.

control

A list of control parameters; see nbreg_control().

weights

Optional non-negative prior weights \(a_i\).

subset

Optional expression selecting the rows of data to use.

na.action

How to handle missing values (default: the na.action option, usually stats::na.omit()).

Value

An object of class "nbreg", a list with components

coefficients

Named vector of estimated \(\beta\).

vcov

Estimated covariance matrix of \(\hat\beta\).

theta, SE.theta

\(\hat\theta\) and its standard error.

log_theta, SE.log_theta

\(\log\hat\theta\) and its standard error (delta method).

loglik

Maximized log-likelihood.

df

Number of estimated parameters (\(p + 1\)).

deviance

Residual deviance at \(\hat\theta\).

iter

Number of outer iterations.

converged

Logical convergence flag.

fitted.values, linear.predictors, residuals

\(\hat\mu_i\), \(\hat\eta_i\), and response residuals \(y_i - \hat\mu_i\).

weights, prior.weights

Final IRLS working weights and the prior weights.

y, offset, nobs, df.residual

Response, offset, number of observations with positive weight, and \(n - p\).

call, formula, terms, model, xlevels, contrasts, na.action, control

Information about the fit.

Algorithm

  1. Starting values. \(\beta\) from a Poisson fit computed by IRLS (working weights \(a_i\mu_i\)); \(\theta\) from the moment estimate \(\sum a_i\mu_i^2 / \sum a_i\{(y_i-\mu_i)^2-\mu_i\}\).

  2. IRLS for \(\beta\) (\(\theta\) fixed): with \(w_i = a_i\mu_i\theta/(\theta+\mu_i)\) and \(z_i = (\eta_i - o_i) + (y_i-\mu_i)/\mu_i\), update \(\beta \leftarrow (X^\top W X)^{-1}X^\top W z\).

  3. Newton-Raphson for \(\phi=\log\theta\) (\(\beta\) fixed): \(\phi \leftarrow \phi - U_\phi/H_\phi\) with \(U_\phi = \theta U(\theta)\) and \(H_\phi = \theta^2 H(\theta) + \theta U(\theta)\).

  4. Repeat 2-3 until the log-likelihood changes by less than control$tol, then do a final IRLS pass at the final \(\theta\).

Standard errors: \(\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat\beta) = (X^\top\hat W X)^{-1}\) (treating \(\theta\) as known) and \(\mathrm{SE}(\hat\theta) = \{-H(\hat\theta)\}^{-1/2}\).

References

Venables, W. N. and Ripley, B. D. (2002). Modern Applied Statistics with S (4th ed.). Springer.

See also

nbreg_control()

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 300
x <- rnorm(n)
y <- rnbinom(n, mu = exp(0.5 + 0.8 * x), size = 2)
fit <- nbreg(y ~ x)
fit$coefficients
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   0.4508058   0.7668655 
fit$theta
#> [1] 1.950002
fit$loglik
#> [1] -526.8916

# with an exposure offset
t <- runif(n, 1, 5)
y2 <- rnbinom(n, mu = t * exp(0.5 + 0.8 * x), size = 2)
nbreg(y2 ~ x, offset = log(t))$coefficients
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   0.5102294   0.6970507
